How is DKA causing Pre- Renal AKI?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; Diabetic Ketoacidosis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003ENocturnal Diuresis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003EDehydration\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003EHypovolemia\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003EAcute Kidney Injury\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E2. Can it be Renal Etiology?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003EYes it can be due to Renal Etiology, existing diabetes cause release of free radicals causing PCT atrophy and damage causing Diabetic Tubulopathy\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E3. Causes and treatment of Tachypnea?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003ETachypnea is a condition that refers to rapid breathing. The normal breathing rate for an average adult is 12 to 20 breaths per minute\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003E.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003ETachypnea\u0026nbsp;does not necessarily have a pathological cause. For example, exercise can cause tachypnea. Some pathological causes of tachypnea are sepsis, diabetic ketoacidosis, respiratory issues such as pneumonia, carbon monoxide poisoning, pulmonary embolism, pleural effusion, asthma, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Other medical issues such as allergic reactions, anxiety states, and foreign body aspiration can also cause tachypnea.\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 15.9991px; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 15.9991px; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E4. Link between LVF and COPD?\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003ELedt sided heart failure is most often caused by high blood pressure or coronary artery disease. It’s not directly related to COPD. But the two conditions may influence each other.\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003EFor example, low oxygen in blood from COPD may put extra strain on your heart which worsens left sided heart failure. And too much fluid in your lungs from heart failure can make breathing even harder if you have COPD\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003E\u003Cfont size=\"4\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont face=\"Times New Roman, serif\" size=\"4\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);\"\u003E5.
